subject: general
question: If X ≥ Y = P > Q ≤ R > Z, which of the following can be concluded?
solution:
**Given statement:** X ≥ Y = P > Q ≤ R > Z

Conclusions:

Option 1) Q ≥ X ≤ Y → Does not follow (As __**X ≥ Y = P > Q**__ ≤ R > Z. So, it can be concluded as 'Q therefore it is false)

Option 2) Z Does not follow (As X ≥ Y = P > __**Q ≤ R > Z**__. Here no relation can be determined between Z and R, therefore it is false)

Option 3) R ≥ Q ≥ P → Does not follow (As X ≥ Y = __**P > Q ≤ R**__ > Z. Here no relation can be determined between P and R, therefore it is false)

Option 4) P ≤ X > Q → Follow (As __**X ≥ Y = P > Q**__ ≤ R > Z. Here, both relations, 'X ≥ P' and 'X > Q' can be determined, therefore is true)

Thus, out of all the options, only 'P ≤ X > Q' can be concluded from the given statement.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 4".
